## Introduction

This experiment will be a replication of Chunharas, 2022[1]. The original focus of their paper was to elucidate functional properties of visual working memory (VWM). The specific goal of experiment 1 was to capture repulsion bias as a functional memory distortion, using a task where participants remember a small set of very similar, yet distinguishable colors. Repulsion serves to make the representations of each color more distinct from one another, while they are held in visual working memory. The first experiment in Chunharas, 2022 consisted of a two-alternative forced choice task (2-AFC) where participants saw two colors, then were asked to recall a target color from 2 colors on screen (one being correct, one being a foil). Experiment 1 yielded very strong evidence for repulsion bias as a feature visual working memory, as participants were "better at rejecting a foil color that was distorted toward the non-target memory item than rejecting a foil color that was distorted away from the non-target memory item" (Chunharas, 2022).

For this replication, the experiment will consist of the same 2-AFC VWM task from Experiment 1 of Chunharas, 2022, still in an online format, but instead using the SONA platform for data collection. The task involves an empty color array with a fixation cross in the center surrounded by 12 empty circles, there will be 2 color samples displayed from the wheel: one "target" color and one non-target color, 45º apart in color space from each other. The participant will then be asked to choose the correct target from two colors, one of which will be a foil either 6º towards the non-target or 6º away from the non-target (in relation to the correct color). The experiment was a within-subjects design where each condition was equally balanced, 60 trials of each type, with 12 catch trials to filter out non-engaged participants. The task code will be recoded in HTML and jsPsych (with the Brady lab's plugins) since the original experiment used MATLAB and Psychophysics toolbox. Thankfully, all of the paper's code was registered via OSF, including the original code for the task, participant data, and analysis code. Following data collection, data analysis will consist of a paired t-tests on accuracy. The original results showed toward vs. away gave t(44)=3.98, p<.001, toward vs. chance gave t(44)=3.73, p=.0006, and away vs. chance gave t(44)=-1.76, p=.08. 

Small note on a possible type in the original paper: The caption for Figure 1c in the text reports the test of toward-foil accuracy against chance as t(44) = 3.73, p = .006. However, a two-sided p-value for t(44) = 3.73 is approximately .0006, and after recomputing the test from original Experiment 1 data file found on OSF gives t(44) = 3.73, p = .00055. Only a small typo, but I thought it was worth noting, since I report .0006 as the p-value in this write-up.

## Methods

I rebuilt Experiment 1 of Chunharas et al. (2022) in jsPsych v8.4 using The Brady Vision and Memory Lab plugins. Participants were presented with two colors 45° apart, that were shown for 150 ms, followed by a 750 ms delay and a two-alternative forced choice (2-AFC) between the cued color and a foil 6° away (toward or away from the non-target color; 60 trials per condition, with 12 catch trials, 132 in total), with responses made via key press. 

### Power Analysis

Effect size not displayed in the original paper, but can be extrapolated from data and figures later. Power analysis for replication sample size is conducted below.

```{r}
library(pwr)

dat <- read.csv("EXP1.csv") # Load Data

acc <- tapply(dat$correct, list(dat$subjects, dat$condition), mean) # Accuracy, per participant, per condition

toward <- acc[, "-6"]   # Assign conditions
away   <- acc[, "6"]
diffs <- toward - away    # Difference Score: toward accuracy - away accuracy
n     <- length(diffs)    # n = 45
cat("Mean difference (toward - away):", round(mean(diffs), 3), "\n")
cat("SD of differences:", round(sd(diffs), 3), "\n")

tt <- t.test(toward, away, paired = TRUE)
tt
```

```{r}
dz <- mean(diffs) / sd(diffs) # Cohen's dz
cat("Cohen's dz:", round(dz, 3), "\n")

t_obs <- mean(diffs) / (sd(diffs) / sqrt(n))   # Observed t
df    <- n - 1
cat("Observed t:", round(t_obs, 3), "\n")

f_lo <- function(ncp) pt(t_obs, df, ncp) - 0.975
f_hi <- function(ncp) pt(t_obs, df, ncp) - 0.025

ncp_lo <- uniroot(f_lo, interval = c(t_obs - 5, t_obs + 5), tol = 1e-8)$root
ncp_hi <- uniroot(f_hi, interval = c(t_obs - 5, t_obs + 5), tol = 1e-8)$root

dz_ci <- c(ncp_lo, ncp_hi) / sqrt(n)
cat("95% CI for dz: [", round(dz_ci[1], 3), ",", round(dz_ci[2], 3), "]\n")
```

```{r}
d_orig <- abs(dz)
sizes  <- c(original = 1, smaller25 = .75, smaller50 = .5)

res <- data.frame(d = d_orig * sizes)

res$n_exact <- sapply(res$d, function(d)
  pwr.t.test(d = d, power = .90, sig.level = .05,
             type = "paired", alternative = "two.sided")$n)

res$n_needed <- ceiling(res$n_exact)
res
```


### Planned Sample

The sample will consist of UC San Diego undergraduates, recruited via the SONA platform and compensated with class credit for their participation (Target n = 60). The anticipated sample will be pre-screened to ensure normal or corrected-to-normal vision without any color-blindness. The larger sample is due to the WEIRD (Western, educated, industrialized, rich, and democratic) nature of the SONA population, as well as extraneous noise that can sometimes occur during online experiments among a busy undergraduate student body. 

### Materials

All materials consist of the code needed to recreate the task, jsPsych plugins from the UCSD Vision and Memory Lab plugins and access to the online SONA platform.

### Procedure	

The task was coded in HTML and Javascript, using jsPsych plugins made by the UCSD Vision and Memory lab. The task display will consist of a 360x360 pixel white background with a 1 pixel wide, with a fixation cross in the center, surrounded by 12 small circular placeholders each centered at a distance of 120 pixels. Each placeholder should have a radius of 20 pixels, and will be 62 pixels apart when measuring center-to-center. There will be 6 placeholders on the left side of the screen, and 6 on the right. There are also two empty placeholders for the response options for the 2-AFC, 35 pixels to the left and right of the fixation cross. Finally, the location probe on screen will be a black circle surrounding where the target color was during the initial exposure. Participants will choose between the two presented colors, using Z to select the left color, and M to select the right color.

The task consisted of showing participants two colors on the color wheel, one "correct" color, and one non-target color, which will always be 45º away in color space from the correct color. There were also 2 empty placeholders between each of the two memory items. Following a 750ms delay, a location cue appears on screen identifying the correct color. This was followed by the two placeholders next to the fixation cross presenting two response options. One response was always the correct color, while the other was always a foil, which differed either by 6º toward the non-target color, or 6º away totaling 132 trials (60 trials each, balanced across conditions, plus 12 catch trials). The position of the correct color on either the left or right of the fixation cross was randomized. The participants were asked to select one of the two color choices on screen on either the left (Z key) or on the right (M key), before advancing.

### Analysis Plan

Data analysis will consist of simply running a paired samples t-test comparing accuracy between the two foil conditions in the 2-AFC task. 

I also plan to visualize the data, and plot novel figures including both participant accuracy by condition, and reaction time.

From original data analysis:

```
setwd("~/yourWorkingDirectory/.../data_codes/R") # <- please change this to your own path

#### EXP1 ####
dat = 'EXP1_subj_fdist_fdirec_val.csv'
datcsv = read.csv(dat, header = FALSE)
colnames(datcsv) = c('subj','fdist','fdirec','val')

datcsv$subj = as.factor(datcsv$subj)
datcsv$fdirec = as.factor(datcsv$fdirec)

# t-test 
t.test(datcsv[datcsv$fdirec==-1,'val']-datcsv[datcsv$fdirec==1,'val'])
``` 

### Differences from Original Study

(1) Experimental Procedure Inconsistencies -- During the recreation of the task's code I followed the original paper’s methods rather than the shared task code found on OSF where the two differed on presentation of stimuli, with one exception noted below. The code placed the two colors at one of 12 fixed location pairs exactly three placeholders apart, added independent ±3° jitter to each item’s hue, and centered the response options ±30 px from fixation. Whereas the paper describes two randomly chosen placeholders with at least two empty placeholders between them, a color separation of exactly 45°, and options at ±35 px. I implemented the paper’s descriptions for the color separation (exactly 45°, no jitter) and for the response options (±35 px). For the item locations I followed the original code instead: the non-target is always exactly three placeholders (90°) from the target, with two empty placeholders between them, and whether it falls clockwise or counter-clockwise of the target is chosen at random on every trial. This satisfies the paper’s “at least two empty placeholders” description, and it keeps the spatial separation between the two items the same on every trial, as in the original task code. Stimulus colors were generated with the color wheel implemented in the original code (L = 65, a = 9, b = 9, radius 50) rather than the parameters reported in the paper (L = 70, a = 20, b = 38, radius 60), because those values fall largely outside the displayable RGB range under the code’s conversion (201 of 360 hues). The location of the target color is also balanced across the 12 placeholders (each placeholder holds the target 10 times, excluding catch trials).

(2) Small Deviations Due to Plugins -- Other differences come from the implementation of the updated plugins: the display box was 360 px rather than 500 px (ring radius and item size matched the paper's design), the target color was probed with a black ring surrounding it, instead of a triangle pointing to it. Fixation was a plus sign preceded by a 2,000 ms fixation interval taken from the original code, and the code was adapted to run participants through SONA rather than MTurk.

(3) Shuffling Bug -- The original task code found on OSF contained a small shuffling error: shuffle() reorders an array in place and returns that same array, so the assignment of target and non-target for each location pair fixed for the whole session. This is to say, before the colors are filled, a pair of locations for initial display (say 0 and 3) are chosen and then randomly assigned to be the target or the non-target color. The shuffling error caused the same location to be assigned to contain the target color for each pair of locations (For location pair 0 and 3, location 3 always contained the target color, it wasn't randomized). In simulations of the original code, on average 3 of the 12 locations were never the target, 6 were the target on 10 of the 120 main trials, and 3 were the target on 20. Our version redraws the locations on every trial, thus the location of the target color is balanced across the 12 locations (10 times for each location).

(4) Miscellaneous -- This new task also included 12 catch trials where the foil is 180° away from the target color, in order to catch online participants who are not engaged with the task. Participants also completed one practice trial at the beginning of the task as a part of the instructions, and moved on whether they answered correctly or not. As well as completing an additional briefing form at the end of the task which included age, gender, and sex assigned at birth. 

(5) Exclusion Criteria -- The original paper didn't list any participant exclusions, as the task itself is made to be difficult (in the original data, mean accuracy was .536 for toward foils and .483 for away foils, about .51 overall). However with our addition of the catch trials (where the correct choice is abundantly clear), we are able to set an exclusion criteria to deal with an online sample where we cannot control for distractions. During data analysis, tests will be conducted on the total population, as well as on a sub-population who answered at least 10 of the 12 catch trials correctly. Since a participant guessing at random would meet this criterion according to a probability of .019.

## Results


### Data preparation/visualization

Data preparation following the analysis plan, along with preliminary figures.
	
```{r}
#### Pre-registered Analysis Code (No data yet, confirmatory analysis run on pilot data)

#### Import data
files <- list.files("raw_data", pattern = "\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)
need  <- c("subject", "trial_kind", "foil_direction", "correct")   
dat   <- do.call(rbind, lapply(files, function(f) read.csv(f, colClasses = "character", na.strings = c("", "NA"))[, need]))
dat$correct <- as.numeric(dat$correct)

#### Data Preparation
main  <- subset(dat, trial_kind == "main")
catch <- subset(dat, trial_kind == "catch")
acc   <- tapply(main$correct, list(main$subject, main$foil_direction), mean)
catch_correct <- as.numeric(tapply(catch$correct, catch$subject, sum)[rownames(acc)])

#### Whole Participant Sample: Paired t-test on accuracy, toward vs. away
t.test(acc[, "toward"], acc[, "away"], paired = TRUE)

#### Exclusion Criteria Sample: Excluding participants with fewer than 10 of 12 catch trials correct
keep <- !is.na(catch_correct) & catch_correct >= 10
t.test(acc[keep, "toward"], acc[keep, "away"], paired = TRUE)

### Assert check
library(assertthat)

assert_that(length(files) == 6)
```
```{r}
### Data Visualization (First attempt)
library(ggplot2)

# Mean accuracy and standard error for each foil condition
df <- data.frame(
  condition = factor(c("Toward", "Away"), levels = c("Toward", "Away")),
  accuracy  = colMeans(acc[, c("toward", "away")]),
  se        = apply(acc[, c("toward", "away")], 2, sd) / sqrt(nrow(acc))
)

ggplot(df, aes(condition, accuracy)) +
  geom_col(fill = c("steelblue", "tomato")) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = accuracy - se, ymax = accuracy + se), width = .2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = "dashed") +   # Chance
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(.3, .7)) +                  # Zoomed in; c(0, 1) is full scope
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Foil direction", y = "Accuracy") +
  theme_classic()
```
```{r}
#### Preliminary Figures (Generated with pilot data)
library(ggplot2)

use <- rep(TRUE, nrow(acc))   # Entire sample
# use <- keep                 # Sample with exclusions

#### Accuracy, toward vs. away  (Error bars = +/-1 SEM across participants)
m    <- acc[use, c("toward", "away")]
sem  <- apply(m - rowMeans(m) + mean(m), 2, sd) / sqrt(nrow(m))
bars <- data.frame(x = 1:2, mean = 100 * (colMeans(m) - .5), sem = 100 * sem, fill = c("tomato", "steelblue"))

ggplot(bars, aes(x)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = x - .4, xmax = x + .4, ymin = -15, ymax = mean, fill = fill), colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = mean - sem, ymax = mean + sem), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:2, labels = c("-6°\ntoward", "+6°\naway")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-15, 15, 5),
                   labels = c("-15%", "-10%", "-5%", "50%\n(chance)", "+5%", "+10%", "+15%")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 2.6), ylim = c(-15, 15), expand = FALSE) +    # Axis fixed at +/-15% to accommodate noisy pilot data
# "Prefer correct color / Prefer foil color" arrows
  annotate("segment", x = .35, xend = .35, y = 4, yend = 12.5, colour = "#46464a", linewidth = 2.2,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(.13, "in"), type = "closed")) +
  annotate("segment", x = .35, xend = .35, y = -4, yend = -12.5, colour = "#46464a", linewidth = 2.2,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(.13, "in"), type = "closed")) +
  annotate("text", x = .27, y = 8,  label = "Prefer\ncorrect\ncolor", hjust = 1, fontface = "bold", size = 3.2, lineheight = .9) +
  annotate("text", x = .27, y = -8, label = "Prefer\nfoil\ncolor",    hjust = 1, fontface = "bold", size = 3.2, lineheight = .9) +
  labs(x = "Foil distance from correct color", y = "Accuracy") +
  theme_classic()

#### Mean RT on every trial, averaged across participants (Error bars = +/-1 SEM across participants)
rt <- na.omit(do.call(rbind, lapply(files, function(f) read.csv(f)[, c("subject", "trial_num", "rt")])))
rt <- rt[rt$subject %in% rownames(acc)[use], ]
by_trial <- data.frame(trial = sort(unique(rt$trial_num)),
                       mean  = tapply(rt$rt, rt$trial_num, mean),
                       sem   = tapply(rt$rt, rt$trial_num, function(v) sd(v) / sqrt(length(v))))

ggplot(by_trial, aes(trial, mean)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = mean - sem, ymax = mean + sem), colour = "#6da7ec") +
  geom_line(colour = "#2a78d6") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(x = "Trial number", y = "Mean reaction time (ms)") +
  theme_classic()
```
